newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Centam ministers to meet with IDB in Guatemala.
newsitem.headline: Centam ministers to meet with IDB in Guatemala.

text.p: Interamerican Development Bank (IDB) President Enrique Iglesias said he will meet Friday in Guatemala with the bank's Central American governors to discuss 1997 loan programs for the region.

"We will discuss some special issues such as improving our offices in the region, specific support programs for regional integration projects and of course we will discuss the issue of electric integration," Iglesias told reporters at a news conference Thursday.
Iglesias said this was a regular meeting held before the IDB's yearly assembly, which is scheduled for March 17 in Barcelona this year.

Participants will include the finance ministers of El Salvador, Costa Rica and Guatemala, the central bank presidents of Guatemala and Belize, the economic cabinet coordinating minister of Honduras, Nicaragua's foreign aid minister, and Panama's planning minister.

Iglesias announced Thursday that the bank will lend Guatemala $330 million in 1997 for a variety of programs linked to this nation's peace process. Guatemala recently ended 36 years of civil war with a peace treaty.
The IDB is the largest financial source for Central America and was continually working on increasing funding for the region, Iglesias said.
The president said the bank was particularly interested in supporting improvements to the Panamerican Highway in each country.
Fifty percent of IDB loans in the region are for social and education programs, he said.
